html:
A band founded in 1956 in Léopoldville, now Kinshasa, led for most of its life by the guitarist and singer Franco Luambo. Under Franco, OK Jazz made Congolese rumba the dance music of much of Africa.

The name came from the OK Bar, where the band first played. Congolese rumba grew from Cuban records that had been popular in the Congo since the 1940s. OK Jazz sang mostly in Lingala and added the "sebene", a fast, looping guitar section that set dancers going. Its great rival was African Jazz, led by Le Grand Kallé.

Over nearly four decades the band, later called TPOK Jazz, "all-powerful OK Jazz", had dozens of members and a huge catalogue. Franco's songs commented on love, money and politics. Some praised Mobutu; others earned him jail. After Franco died in 1989 the band carried on for a few years and broke up in 1993. In 2021 Congolese rumba was added to UNESCO's list of the world's living heritage.
sum: A band founded in 1956 in Léopoldville, now Kinshasa, led for most of its life by the guitarist and singer Franco Luambo. Under Franco, OK Jazz made Congolese rumba the dance music of much of Africa.
